title: Swiss Glaciers Lose More Ice in 2026
paragraphs: Switzerland's glaciers have weathered yet another punishing year. The annual report of the Glacier Monitoring Switzerland network (GLAMOS), published on 1 October, puts the 2026 loss at more than 5 percent of total ice volume: short of the record set in 2022, yet one more entry in a ledger that now shows nearly a fifth of the country's glacier ice gone in just five years.

The ice was undone by a double blow. A winter among the ten least snowy since measurements began stripped the glaciers of their protective blanket, and a sweltering summer finished the job, with the freezing level climbing above 4,000 metres on 76 days, more than twice the norm and a Swiss record. From July to September, the glaciers shed roughly 2,200 billion litres of meltwater, over four times what Swiss households drink in a year, a windfall for the rivers that is, by its nature, a one-off.

The casualties are small in scale but large in symbolism: Bella Tola in Valais and Griessfirn in Glarus have vanished outright, while the Rhône, Aletsch and Clariden glaciers endured their heaviest melt on record. As a monitoring report from a single country, the document measures the damage with precision but is not designed to apportion blame among its causes, a task that falls to other research.

questions.q: What does "a ledger" suggest about the way the losses are described?
questions.a: Each year's loss is recorded and adds to a running total.

questions.q: Why does the author call the extra meltwater a "one-off" windfall?
questions.a: Because it comes from ice that will not be there to melt again.

questions.q: What kind of task is left to other research?
questions.a: Working out how much each cause contributed to the melt.
